questions.answer: Convoluted and contra-intuitive. Ask for help.

questions.answer: The best way to get help is to ask. Find out who's responsible and write them and email or show up in their office, if you can find it. They're probably nice.

questions.answer: There was no group work, everything was discussed in plenum. Also, the professors seemingly had more authority.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I will say that food really is much cheaper in Germany than in Denmark. I was surprised sometimes. Also, at the universities in Berlin you pay a one time fee (about 1,200.00) to have transportation for the full semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take advantage of your unlimited public transportation that your Deutschland Semester Ticket allows for and go everywhere. Just take the train, the bus, or the u-bahn and explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Maybe take up smoking and meet people outside. Otherwise, I would recommend finding out what interests you and going there. Do you like art? Go to gallery openings and meet people there. Do you like music? Go to concerts. Do you like sports? Go to football games and talk to people there. It's easier to talk to people you've met through common interests. But of course it can be nerve-wrecking to go to events on your own and talking to strangers. But it's worth it.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You will be surprised, annoyed, and fascinated by how impractical, convoluted, contra-intuitive, and plain stupid their overly bureaucratic and non-digitalized systems are. And by how many people (at least the one's who aren't university students) don't really speak English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The many small independent galleries and concert venues.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Take advantage of the German language courses they offer. The teachers are great. 
- Go to all the things, you feel could be interesting. The exchange is over so quickly, take advantage of every opportunity. 
- Eat in the mensa even though the food is often questionable. When you get back you will have a lot of fun stories about grotesque abberations of culinary customs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No just have fun.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made along the way<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I had to go home again. Really, it was amazing and I wanted to stay.

questions.answer: Yes
